text: You're hyped for an event – concert, game. You imagine that perfect seat, right in the action. You just want the best view, an amazing experience.
But when tickets drop? Those prime spots vanish instantly. Or they're so expensive, completely out of reach. You're left with less exciting, far-back options.
It’s confusing. Why do the best seats always disappear first? Is it bad luck? Or are certain people getting special access? It feels so unfair.
The invisible system is differential pricing. Organizers know some fans pay a premium for prime locations, others prioritize value over the absolute best spot.
So, the most desirable seats are priced highest, selling first to maximize revenue. Other price tiers then fill with different customer segments at lower costs.
You’re not unlucky; you’re observing a calculated strategy. Now, when best seats vanish, you’ll understand the market at work, not just bad timing.
